item.title: Defence min says a 'hybrid model' of army, govt runs Pak
item.description: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif defended the nation's 'hybrid model' of governance, where military and civilian leaders share power, despite its poor democratic record. Confronted by Mehdi Hasan about the military's true authority, Asif rejected dominance claims. He labeled the US system a "deep state" and blamed past military rulers for Pakistan's perception.

item.title: Over my dead body, says Soros' son as Trump admin focuses on $23 billion charity
item.description: Alex Soros, leading the Open Society Foundations, defiantly stated in New York that his $23 billion philanthropic organisation would not yield to President Trump's pressure. This declaration followed reports of a Justice Department investigation into OSF, which Soros vowed would continue its human rights work, amidst broader administration efforts targeting Democrat-aligned groups and their infrastructure.

item.title: Colombia President Gustavo Petro shrugs off US cancellation of his visa
item.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro's US visa was revoked following his participation in a pro-Palestine protest at the UN General Assembly. Petro dismissed the decision, citing his Italian citizenship and global identity. The US State Department attributed the cancellation to "reckless and incendiary actions," while a consultant suggested it politically benefits Petro by framing him as a persecuted, brave voice.

item.title: Slovakia resists push to quickly quit Russian oil
item.description: Slovakia's President Peter Pellegrini informed Donald Trump that his nation will not swiftly abandon Russian oil supplies. Despite Trump's pressure on EU holdouts to cut Moscow's war funding, Slovakia cites technological hurdles and limited alternative routes. Pellegrini emphasized the need for diversification, seeking multiple energy sources rather than replacing Russian dependence with American.

item.title: Curbs set to 'snap back'; Iran recalls envoys to France, Britain, Germany
item.description: Iran has recalled its ambassadors to France, Britain, and Germany after the E3 nations triggered a mechanism to reinstate international sanctions on Tehran. The Iranian foreign ministry condemned this "irresponsible" decision, summoning the envoys for consultations. This move follows the E3's formal invocation of the "snapback" mechanism, potentially reimposing UN sanctions within 30 days.

item.title: Russian minister Lavrov to UN: No intention of attacking Europe
IBSA slams Israel's 'use of starvation' as war strategy
item.description: India, Brazil, and South Africa, under the IBSA grouping, strongly condemned Israeli attacks on Gaza during a UN General Assembly meeting. They expressed grave concern over the "occupied" Palestinian territory, deploring the use of starvation as a method of warfare. The nations called for a permanent ceasefire, Israeli troop withdrawal, and Hamas to release remaining hostages, citing unprecedented civilian suffering.

item.title: Fastest-selling cars in US are used EVs
item.description: Used electric vehicles are now almost as cheap as used gas cars and selling faster, with sales up 34% this year. Significant discounts, like a Ford Mustang Mach-E GT bought for $33,000, are attracting buyers. This trend is fueled by EVs' low maintenance and durable, warranted batteries.

item.title: FBI fires agents who kneeled at 2020 racial justice protest
item.description: WASHINGTON: The FBI has reportedly fired agents who were photographed kneeling during a 2020 racial justice protest in Washington, sparked by George Floyd's killing. This action follows a series of dismissals within the agency since Trump loyalist Kash Patel took over as FBI chief in February.

item.title: Boeing settles lawsuit linked to deceased whistleblower
item.description: Boeing settled a wrongful death lawsuit with the mother of John Barnett, a former employee who raised production concerns. The company agreed to pay at least $50,000, and Barnett's mother dropped claims that Boeing contributed to his suicide. The settlement also resolves a retaliation claim, with Boeing expressing condolences.

item.title: 996 hustle culture is taking hold in Silicon Valley
item.description: Silicon Valley is embracing the "996" work culture, mirroring China's intense tech scene, with employees working 9 am to 9 pm, six days a week. This shift, driven by AI investments and post-layoff insecurity, signals a new "hard tech" era where extreme hours are becoming the norm, perpetuating a long-standing, demanding industry culture.

item.title: Dubai Police stern warning to fans ahead of India-Pakistan Asia Cup final: Strict rules, banned items, Rs 7 lakh fine, jail penalties!
item.description: For the first time in 41 years, India and Pakistan face off in the Asia Cup final at Dubai International Stadium on September 28. With India unbeaten and Pakistan determined, Dubai authorities have tightened security, issued strict guidelines, and warned of legal penalties to ensure safety. Fans are urged to cooperate, follow rules, and uphold sportsmanship for a smooth, historic event.

item.title: UAE Media Chief meets Elon Musk at Tesla HQ, invites him to Abu Dhabi BRIDGE Summit
item.description: UAE media chairman Abdulla Al Hamed met Elon Musk at Tesla HQ on September 27, 2025, extending an invitation to the inaugural BRIDGE Summit in Abu Dhabi. Their discussions centred on AI, data centres, and clean energy's role in future technology.

item.title: Canada woos US H-1B holders: PM Carney says he will soon roll out an offer
item.description: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney announced plans to attract skilled foreign workers, particularly those to be impacted by the US's new $100,000 H-1B visa fee. Recognizing these individuals as enterprising, Canada aims to capitalize on this opportunity. Indians already form Canada's largest immigrant group, with thousands becoming permanent residents and citizens annually.
